Just hit you Hair with your blow dryer as you re-style and the wax does all the work for you. It easily washes from my hair with normal shampooing but I do use a clairifing shampoo once a week as well.

I recently got a very short pixie cut after having shoulder length or longer hair most of my life. This wax was mentioned on a YouTube video I watched. After trying a few other ones, this one is better by far. The hold is flexible enough for touch ups during the day (or even next day!). It warms up and spreads nicely on my hands for even distribution exactly where I need it. My hair doesn’t look gloopy or greasy like another wax/pomade I tried.

Don’t use too much. Rub hands together and product gets warm. Place it on roots where you want lift. Rub hands again and put on tips of fingers and do hair ends If you don’t wash your hair every day you can use a blow dryer to reactivate Works really good.

reviews.t: If you want news anchor hair this is your product
reviews.x: I buy this for my husband who loves hair products. He was getting one from Dollar Shave Club that he can no longer get. I heard a local talk show host saying he used this product. Since my husband likes his hair to look like a news anchor it seemed like something he'd like. I was right. I like that fact that even when he's a little heavy handed with the product, it doesn't look like a helmet. He likes it better than the DSC product he was getting. Great hold and feel.

claims.text: Reviewers widely praise the product for holding short, spiky, and pixie styles well.
Many reviewers note the wax is not greasy and does not weigh hair down, working well on fine or thin hair.
Several reviewers mention the wax is very hard or firm and needs warming or rubbing to soften before use.
A few reviewers note build-up or the need for clarifying shampoo, and some find it expensive.
One reviewer received an old, dried-up, rancid product.
